newsitem.title: FINLAND: NIINISTO SAYS CEN BANK TO DO STATE FOREX PURCHASES.
newsitem.headline: NIINISTO SAYS CEN BANK TO DO STATE FOREX PURCHASES.

text.p: Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Wednesday the Bank of Finland would, despite an announced policy change, still take care of foreign currency purchases for state debt servicing needs on the forex market.

Asked by a Reuters reporter to clarify a new policy according to which the state would go directly to the currency markets to obtain foreign exchange needed for foreign debt service instead of buying these currencies from the central bank, Niinisto said the central bank would continue to handle "the technical side" of the transactions.
"But it will not come from central bank reserves," he said.
"It is a question of nuance ... who is handling the technical implementation," he added.
The finance ministry would not take care of the actual foreign currency purchases "for practical reasons," he said, but did not elaborate.

Niinisto said the policy shift away from government foreign currency denominated debt servicing via the central bank's foreign currency reserves was a strong signal despite the fact that the Bank of Finland would handle the market purchases.
"It is a clear message that there will be a big buyer which is not the central bank," he said.
Asked how other market operators would be able to know whether the Bank of Finland, when in the market, was acting for its own reasons or on behalf of the state, Niinisto said:

"I think the distinction will become clear ... it can be seen later and the delay is not very long." He was referring to the central bank's weekly balance sheet, which also details changes in foreign currency reserves.
The state's amortisation and interest costs on the foreign currency debt would be 42 billion markka this year, Niinisto said in a statement on Tuesday.
